variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, NP_000220.1:p.(Arg322Cys). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; the review does not name the original publication in the row, so the person-level data are second-hand.
Zygosity, phase and family data are not given in the review; the batch row records zygosity as not reported.
Only one LCAT variant listed for a recessive disease; zygosity not stated, so the person may be a heterozygous carrier.
notes_for_panel: One unclassified Dutch male (author Holleboom), single LCAT variant listed, zygosity not stated. Tabulated LCAT activity 73 nmol/mL/h; the review's FED group median is given elsewhere as 41.5 nmol/mL/h, but no reference range is given for this row. With only one allele listed, this may be a heterozygous carrier ascertained for low HDL-C; the review does not say.
